### Purpose
The contribution's purpose is to "speed up inference of flow-matching heads in autoregressive image generation." Paper [1] explicitly addresses accelerating flow-matching models, stating: "We propose FastFlow, a plug-and-play adaptive inference framework that accelerates generation in flow matching models." Paper [12] also targets inference acceleration for autoregressive image generation, stating: "We introduce Grouped Speculative Decoding (GSD), a novel, training-free acceleration method for AR image models." Both papers share the same objective of inference acceleration for flow-matching or autoregressive models, making the purpose covered.

### Mechanism
The contribution mechanism, Velocity-Forecast Sampling (VFS), speculatively reuses velocity predictions across ODE steps, verifying via MSE-based drift detection and falling back to standard sampling on rejection. Paper [4] describes a training-free conditional sampling method for flow matching models using importance sampling and resampling techniques, which shares the primitive of training-free acceleration for flow-matching models. Paper [12] introduces speculative decoding for autoregressive image generation, which involves draft generation and verification, sharing the speculative reuse and fallback primitive. Paper [18] discusses relaxed speculative decoding for autoregressive image generation, which similarly involves speculative acceleration with fallback mechanisms. These papers collectively cover the mechanism.

### Evaluation
The contribution evaluates VFS on NextStep-1.1 with GenEval, achieving competitive speedup and moderate quality scores. Paper [12] evaluates Grouped Speculative Decoding (GSD) for autoregressive image generation using standard benchmarks and metrics, sharing the speculative decoding evaluation design. Paper [18] evaluates relaxed speculative decoding using theoretical analysis and empirical benchmarks, also sharing the speculative decoding evaluation design. Both papers reuse speculative decoding evaluation designs, making the evaluation covered.

### Domain
The contribution operates in the domain of inference acceleration for flow-matching heads in autoregressive image generation. Paper [1] explicitly addresses inference acceleration for flow-matching models, stating: "FastFlow identifies denoising steps that produce only negligible changes and skips them." Paper [12] targets autoregressive image generation acceleration, stating: "We introduce Grouped Speculative Decoding (GSD), a novel, training-free acceleration method for AR image models." Both papers work in the same general application area, making the domain covered.

Paper [1] describes "plug-and-play adaptive inference framework that accelerates generation in flow matching models" by "identifying denoising steps that produce only [small changes]" — this is substantively equivalent: training-free reuse of flow-matching computations based on detected redundancy. The combination of speculative reuse + MSE verification + fallback in flow matching is most directly covered by [1] (adaptive reuse in flow matching) and [20] (cache-and-verify with error threshold).

The contribution analyzes two limiting factors: classifier-free guidance (CFG) disrupting velocity-field smoothness and the flow-matching (FM) head being a small share of latency. Paper [3] discusses flow matching in the context of visual synthesis acceleration, and [10] addresses FM head efficiency challenges. These papers collectively cover the primitives of CFG's impact on smoothness and FM head latency, even if they do not combine them in the same analysis.

The contribution evaluates CFG acceptance rates (12-21% per step) and FM head latency (~31% of per-token latency, capping speedup at ~1.45x). Papers [3], [8], [10], and [17] evaluate flow matching and diffusion models using similar metrics and validation setups, such as latency analysis and speedup quantification. Papers [1], [5], [6], and [9] evaluate CFG mechanisms, including acceptance rates and their impact on generation quality. These prior works collectively cover the evaluation design, even if applied to different benchmarks or objects.

### Domain
The contribution operates in the domain of inference acceleration for flow-matching heads in autoregressive image generation. Papers [3], [10], and [17] address flow matching and diffusion models in the context of generative image synthesis, which is the same general application area.
